extraction.name: WikiText
extraction.description: A benchmark corpus for language modeling designed to evaluate how well language models can exploit longer contexts and handle more realistic vocabularies and larger corpora. It is introduced as a freely available alternative to the Penn Treebank.
extraction.creator: Stephen Merity, Caiming Xiong, James Bradbury, Richard Socher
extraction.rai:dataCollection: We constructed a language modeling dataset using text extracted from Wikipedia. We selected articles only fitting the Good or Featured article criteria specified by editors on Wikipedia, then extracted the text for each article using the Wikipedia API. Specific sections which primarily featured lists were removed by default, and other minor bugs were removed. Mathematical formulae and LaTeX code were replaced with token placeholders. Normalization and tokenization were performed using the Moses tokenizer, and words below a frequency threshold were discarded with out-of-vocabulary words mapped to a special token.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Words outside of the vocabulary were mapped to the hunkitoken; the vocabulary was constructed by discarding all words with a count below 3.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Wikipedia articles fitting the Good or Featured article criteria; text extracted from Wikipedia markup.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Articles were selected only if they fit Good or Featured article criteria; sections primarily featuring lists were removed; minor HTML bugs like sort keys and Edit buttons were removed; mathematical formulae and LaTeX code were replaced with <formula> tokens; normalization and tokenization were performed using the Moses tokenizer; numbers were further split; words below count 3 were discarded; out-of-vocabulary words were mapped to <unk>.
